### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
No switch; identities apply when the selected maps exist and floors do not change the state.
The temperature floor requires consistent energy recovery.
The enthalpy identity is @eq-ch02-consistency-enthalpy.
:::

### Derivation

At fixed conserved partial densities, adding constant-capacity species energies gives

$$
\rho e(T)=\rho_{\mathrm d}u_{\mathrm d}^\star+\sum_n\rho_nu_n^\star
+\left(\rho_{\mathrm d}c_{v,\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nc_{v,n}\right)T
$$ {#eq-ch02-consistency-affine}

@eq-ch02-consistency-affine is implemented by `_temp2intEng` in [`ideal_moist.cpp:293-317`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L293-L317).

Thus the zero-temperature intercept is the offset, and the slope includes the dry heat capacity. Substituting
the temperature recovered from pressure reproduces `W->I`. Integrating over a uniform cell merely multiplies
this identity by $V_i$. For temperature-dependent capacities, `UT->I` evaluates the same `VT->U` function
as `W->I`, rather than assuming affinity.

The code's `species_enthalpy` returns thermodynamic enthalpy plus specific kinetic energy, and excludes the dry
row. Adding that dry contribution explicitly, and summing gas pressure shares, gives

$$
\rho_{\mathrm d}\left(\hat h_{\mathrm d}+\tfrac12\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2\right)
+\sum_n\rho_n\left(\hat h_n+\tfrac12\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2\right)=E+p
$$ {#eq-ch02-consistency-enthalpy}

@eq-ch02-consistency-enthalpy is implemented by `species_enthalpy` in [`ideal_moist.cpp:260-280`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L260-L280).

The first part of the sum is internal energy plus pressure; the remaining mass-weighted kinetic terms sum to
$\tfrac12\rho|\mathbf v|^2$. This proves the identity and explains why condensates must have no pressure share.
`consistency_check.py` verifies the intercept, temperature round trip and enthalpy sum independently.
Exactness is algebraic for the specified energy functions; floors and incomplete Newton convergence break
an inverse-map claim.

### Numerical method

The conserved limiter asks `UT->I` for a minimum internal energy at its configured temperature.
Using a different offset or omitting the dry heat capacity would enforce a different temperature.
Species tables must belong to the EOS instance; cloud-parent lookup and sedimentation must not resolve
indices against a subsequently replaced global table. These are local data-ownership requirements, not
a spatial accuracy improvement.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A dedicated moist-mixture `UT->I` versus `W->I` regression is still needed. The existing temperature-sweep
script selects ideal-moist only. Algebraic reuse of `VT->U` is not a replacement for a compiled test.
Switch-combination coverage remains pending in @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
